The Goffertstadion was buzzing with anticipation for this UEFA Champions League clash on August 11, 2026 . What unfolded was a gripping narrative of resilience, tactical shifts, and late-game heroics that kept the spectators on the edge of their seats until the very last whistle. A Tactical Battle Marred by Early Injuries The match began with a cagey atmosphere as both sides looked to establish dominance. However, the rhythm was frequently disrupted by physical challenges and early injury concerns. Dani Garcia picked up an early booking for Olympiakos , setting a physical tone. By the 34th minute, both managers had already been forced into multiple substitutions; Konstantinos Fortounis replaced Jota Silva for the visitors, while NEC Nijmegen saw Emre Mor and Brayann Pereira enter the fray for Sami Ouaissa and Philippe Sandler respectively. Deadlock Broken and a Costly Red Card The second half exploded into life almost immediately. In the 46th minute, Ayoub El Kaabi silenced the home crowd, finishing clinically to give Olympiakos a 0-1 lead. The Dutch side responded with vigor, and after a series of yellow cards for the visitors, the pressure finally told. In the 70th minute, Clement Bischoff turned provider, finding Bryan Linssen who slotted home the equalizer to restore parity. As the game entered its final stretch, a massive turning point arrived. In the 80th minute, Konstantinos Fortounis was shown a straight red card. The decision sparked heavy protests from the Olympiakos players, but the referee remained unmoved. Down to ten men, the Greek giants were forced into a defensive shell as the match headed into a tension-filled extra-time period. Emre Mor Seals the Victory With the numerical advantage, NEC Nijmegen pushed for the winner, and it didn't take long to arrive. In the 95th minute, Kaj Sierhuis —who had been booked just moments earlier in stoppage time—delivered a pinpoint assist for Emre Mor . The substitute made no mistake, firing the ball into the net to make it 2-1. Despite a flurry of late substitutions and a yellow card for Bruno Onyemaechi , Olympiakos could not find a way back into the match. The final whistle confirmed a famous victory for NEC Nijmegen , as they capitalized on their extra man to secure all three points in a memorable European night.
